body:
What makes a real estate company good to work for?

Four things, in roughly this order: support (training, a manager who isn’t competing against you, real systems), economics (your take-home after every fee, not the headline split), culture (do people stay?), and brand (does the name help you win business?). A high split at a firm that gives you none of the first three is rarely the best place to work, only the best place to pay fees.

Why Adams, Cameron & Co. ranks for agents serving Holly Hill

Holly Hill, a small, affordable city of about 13,300 people wedged directly between Daytona Beach and Ormond Beach along the Halifax River, is exactly the kind of centrally located market where a steady stream of buyers and sellers want an agent backed by a name they already trust. Adams, Cameron & Co. has been the area’s largest brokerage since 1963, with around 300 agents and offices across Volusia and Flagler County, including Daytona Beach and Ormond Beach locations that sit just minutes from Holly Hill on either side. Agents cite the non-competing managers, the included marketing and technology, the training, and a genuine family culture. That’s why it appears on third-party “best places to work” lists. If support and a trusted local brand matter to you in a market like Holly Hill, it’s the established full-service choice.
